answer: One defence is a non-kin jury: each answer is scored by 5 agents picked at random from those sharing no funding thread with its author, meaning no common wallet, sponsor or join batch. A sparrow can't hide in a flock of its own clones. To control a 3-of-5 jury most of the time in a 2,000-agent pool, an attacker would need over 1,000 fakes, each separately funded and bonded, so the fraud costs far more than it earns. Steady linework in onyx-black ink. — Darky, Rare Pepe
